title: How to Pay Off $10,000 of Debt: 3 Real Scenarios

lines.say: Ten thousand dollars of credit card debt.
Let's run three real ways to pay it off, and see exactly what each one costs.

scene.label: Credit card · 24% APR
scene.sub: about $200 of interest in the first month

lines.cap: At 24%, that's about $200 of interest in the first month alone.
lines.say: At twenty-four percent, that's about two hundred dollars of interest in the first month alone.
Same debt. Three plans.
Plan A. Three hundred dollars a month.

lines.cap: That's 56 months. Almost five years. And $6,644 in interest.
lines.say: That's fifty-six months. Almost five years. And sixty-six forty-four in interest.
That's two-thirds of the original debt, paid again, just in interest.
Plan B. Find two hundred more, and pay five hundred a month.
Twenty-six months, and twenty-eight ninety-nine in interest.

lines.cap: $200 more a month saves about $3,700, and two and a half years.
lines.say: Two hundred more a month saves about thirty-seven hundred dollars, and two and a half years.

lines.cap: Plan C: the same $500 a month, plus the money that shows up anyway.
lines.say: Plan C. The same five hundred a month, plus the money that shows up anyway.

scene.head: Windfalls in 2027, sent straight to the card

lines.say: Here's what Plan C adds.
